Parameter: Population exposure normalisation method and reference bounds
Options_Considered: (A) Min-max across study area (all communities); (B) Min-max per state; (C) Percentile rank; (D) Fixed thresholds
Decision: Min-max across the full study area (all 10 states combined). Reference bounds fixed at baseline population values — do not recalculate at each update cycle.
Rationale: Study-area-wide normalisation enables cross-state comparison — a primary analytical need. Fixing reference bounds at baseline ensures scores are stable across update cycles. Per-state normalisation would make scores incomparable across states. Population values are from DB01 at the time of baseline publication.
Sensitivity_Note: Compute sensitivity using per-state normalisation as alternative; report rank correlation between methods
Notes: Reference bounds: Min = 0 (community with no population in hazard zone); Max = highest Pop_in_Moderate_Plus_Hazard value across all study communities at baseline. If a new community is added in an update cycle its score is computed using the FROZEN baseline reference bounds — only a new baseline publication resets bounds.

Options_Considered: (A) Simple count of all infrastructure items; (B) Count of critical infrastructure only; (C) Weighted count (critical items weighted higher); (D) Road-length-weighted score
Decision: Weighted count: Critical_Infra_Exposed × 3 + Critical_Roads_km × 2 + Buildings_Exposed × 1 + POI_Critical_Exposed × 3. Normalise weighted sum to 0-100 using study-area reference bounds.
Rationale: Critical infrastructure (hospitals; water supply; federal roads) has disproportionate impact when disrupted. Weighting reflects relative community-level consequence of loss. Equal weighting undervalues critical facilities. Weights must be approved before computation.
Sensitivity_Note: Run with equal weights (weight = 1 for all components) as sensitivity check — report rank correlation
Notes: Weights (3/2/1/3) are indicative — must be formally approved before computation. If weighting scheme is changed a new model version must be created. These weights apply to IND06 infrastructure exposure component only.

Parameter: Erosion exposure threat buffer and severity weighting
Options_Considered: (A) Simple count of assets in buffer; (B) Severity-weighted count (asset_count × site_severity); (C) Distance-decayed exposure; (D) Binary in/out buffer
Decision: Severity-weighted count: sum of (asset_count × Severity_0_4) for all active erosion sites within 5km of community. Buffer for asset identification = BUF003 (100m). Severity weighting reflects the larger threat posed by high-severity sites.
Rationale: A community adjacent to a Severity_4 gully faces fundamentally greater threat than one adjacent to a Severity_1 rill. Ignoring severity in exposure scoring loses important hazard information. The 5km community proximity radius is distinct from the 100m asset threat buffer — the former identifies which communities are relevant; the latter identifies which specific assets are exposed.
Sensitivity_Note: Run with unweighted count (severity weight = 1 for all sites) as sensitivity; report rank correlation
Notes: The 5km community proximity radius for identifying relevant erosion sites is based on BUF005 (community service radius). The 100m asset threat buffer is BUF003. Both come from BUFFER_RULES.csv. Do not change buffer distances without updating BUFFER_RULES.csv.

Parameter: Minimum data threshold for publishing exposure scores
Options_Considered: (A) Publish all communities regardless of data completeness; (B) Publish only Full completeness communities; (C) Publish all but flag Partial and Minimal with caution statement
Decision: Publish all communities with Exposure_Data_Completeness populated. Flag Partial and Minimal communities with explicit data confidence rating in outputs. Do not suppress Minimal communities — their limited data is itself informative for resource allocation.
Rationale: Suppressing communities with incomplete data would create blind spots in priority analysis. Decision-makers need to know where data is weak. Partial and Minimal exposure scores are indicative only — this must be stated in every output using them.
Notes: Exposure_Data_Completeness field is mandatory in both G29 and G30. Any output (map/table/report) using exposure scores must display the completeness category alongside the score. A community with Completeness = None should be shown as 'No data' not 0.

Parameter: Unit of analysis for exposure aggregation
Options_Considered: (A) Community only; (B) LGA only; (C) Both community and LGA; (D) Community + LGA + State
Decision: Community as primary unit of analysis. Aggregate to LGA and State for reporting. Retain community-level scores in all published datasets to preserve traceability.
Rationale: The community is the operational unit for intervention planning. LGA and state aggregations are required for policy reporting but must not obscure community-level variation. The specification explicitly requires outputs by community/LGA/state/asset type.
Notes: LGA aggregation: population-weighted mean of community scores within the LGA. State aggregation: population-weighted mean of LGA scores within the state. Document aggregation method in processing notes.

Options_Considered: (A) Include socio-economic variables in exposure; (B) Exclude all vulnerability variables from exposure
Decision: Exclude all socio-economic vulnerability variables from G29 and G30. Exposure = physical assets and population in hazard zone only. Vulnerability is computed separately in G33.
Rationale: The HEVC framework (Hazard × Exposure × Vulnerability × Criticality) requires clean separation of components. Mixing vulnerability into exposure creates double-counting in the composite risk index (G35). Adaptive capacity; income; education; social deprivation all belong in G33 — not in G29 or G30.
Notes: This is a NON-NEGOTIABLE architectural rule. It is enforced by QC checks G29-Q17 and G30-Q17. Any analyst proposing to add vulnerability variables to G29/G30 must be redirected to G33.
